about.title: Adelanto Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Adelanto's traffic pulls from Rt 395, Bellflower Street, Palmdale Road, and Air Expwy, corridors that carry a steady mix of local and through traffic across this High Desert community of roughly 33,000 residents. San Bernardino County records show 59 injury collisions and 92 injured people in the most recent final crash year, with reported crashes clustering on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. That pattern often means end-of-week commuters heading home or out for the evening. Whatever the circumstances of your crash, the days right after matter: photos, witness names, and vehicle damage can fade or disappear quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves, but we can connect you with an independent attorney in our network who handles cases like yours on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless there's a recovery. Reaching out early gives you the best chance to preserve what evidence exists.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer Calls

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but claims against a government entity (like a city road issue) can require notice in as little as six months. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies to your Adelanto crash.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Your Recovery
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly blamed for the collision, you may still recover a reduced amount. An early, careful review of the facts helps make sure fault isn't unfairly pinned on you.

items.title: Skip the Recorded Statement
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement quickly, before you know the full extent of your injuries. You're not required to give one, and an attorney can speak for you while evidence from the scene is still fresh.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Adelanto?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, such as San Bernardino County or the City of Adelanto, was involved in causing the crash (for example, a road or signal issue), the notice deadline can be as short as six months. It's worth confirming your specific deadline early so you don't lose the right to pursue a claim.

items.question: What if the accident happened on Rt 395 or Palmdale Road and I wasn't sure who was at fault?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the collision, though your recovery may be reduced by your percentage of fault. Corridors like Rt 395 and Palmdale Road see a range of traffic patterns, so an early investigation matters. An independent attorney can help sort out what happened and how fault should be allocated.

items.question: Should I talk to the other driver's insurance company first?
items.answer: You're not obligated to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often better to hold off until you've spoken with an attorney. Early statements can be used against you later, especially before you know the full scope of your injuries. LawProactive can connect you with an attorney who can communicate with the insurer on your behalf.
